Content: A landscaper needs to determine the height of a mature oak tree but doesn't have a tall enough ladder. At `text(3:00 PM)`, the landscaper, who is exactly `text(6 feet)` tall, casts a shadow that is `text(8 feet)` long. At the exact same time, the oak tree casts a shadow that is `text(32 feet)` long on the flat ground.
Assuming the sun's rays create similar right triangles, what is the height of the oak tree, in ``text(feet)``?

A structural engineer uses `text(two)` congruent triangular steel plates to reinforce opposite sides of a bridge joint. The `text(first)` plate has interior angles measuring `42°`, `65°`, and `73°`. The `text(second)` plate has an angle measuring `(3x+10)°` that corresponds perfectly to the `73°` angle of the `text(first)` plate.
What is the value of `x`?

A surveyor places a flat mirror on the ground `text(5 feet)` away from where she is standing. Looking down at the mirror, she can perfectly see the top of a flagpole that is located `text(45 feet)` away from the mirror on the same flat line. The surveyor's eyes are exactly `text(6 feet)` above the ground. Due to the law of reflection, the two triangles formed by the ground, the vertical heights, and the sightlines are similar.
What is the height of the flagpole, in `text(feet)`?

A tailor cuts `text(two)` congruent triangular patches to sew side-by-side into a quilt. The `text(first)` patch has side lengths of `text(15 inches)`, `text(20 inches)`, and `text(25 inches)`. The corresponding sides of the `text(second)` patch have lengths of `text(15 inches)`, `text(20 inches)`, and `(4y-3)` `text(inches)`.
What is the value of `y`?

A primary roof truss forms an isosceles triangle with a horizontal base of `text(24 feet)` and a vertical center height of `text(8 feet)`. A secondary decorative truss over the garage is built to be mathematically similar to the primary truss.
If the decorative truss has a horizontal base of `text(9 feet)`, what is its vertical center height, in `text(feet)`?

A carpenter builds a rectangular wooden gate and reinforces it with `text(two)` diagonal cross-braces that intersect exactly in the middle. This divides the rectangle into `text(four)` triangles. Properties of rectangles dictate that the top triangle and the bottom triangle are congruent.

If the top triangle has a horizontal base of `text(40 inches)` and `text(two)` angled sides that are each `text(29 inches)` long, what is the total perimeter of the bottom triangle, in `text(inches)`?

A carpenter builds a wooden skateboard ramp. The ramp forms a right triangle with a horizontal length of `text(12 feet)` and a vertical height of `text(4 feet)`. A local skate park orders a larger, similar ramp with a horizontal length of `text(30 feet)`.
What is the vertical height of the larger ramp, in `text(feet)`?

A digital projector casts an image onto a theater screen. The light beam originates from a `text(single)` point and spreads outward, forming a triangle. When the screen is `text(8 feet)` away from the projector lens, the image is `text(6 feet)` wide.
If the theater owner moves the projector straight back so it is exactly `text(12 feet)` away from the screen, what will be the new width of the projected image, in `text(feet)`?

A graphic designer creates a logo featuring `text(two)` overlapping right triangles that are geometrically congruent. In the `text(first)` right triangle, the smaller acute angle is `28°`. In the `text(second)` right triangle, the corresponding larger acute angle is represented by the expression `(z/2+10)°`.
What is the value of `z`?

A physics student builds a pinhole camera. The light from a distant object passes through a tiny pinhole, forming an inverted image on the sensor pad at the back of the camera. The distance from the pinhole to the sensor is `text(4 cm)`. The object being photographed is a flower that is `text(15 cm)` tall, located exactly `text(60 cm)` away from the pinhole.
Assuming the light rays form similar triangles on either side of the pinhole, what is the height of the inverted image on the sensor, in `text(centimeters)`?
